stemMd: A password has two letters followed by one digit. Letters are chosen from A, B and C without repetition; the digit is chosen from 0 through 4. How many passwords are possible?
explanationMd: There are three choices for the first letter and two remaining for the second, giving six ordered pairs. Each can be followed by any of five digits. Multiplication gives 3 × 2 × 5 = 30.

distractorRationale.b: This ignores the ordering of the two different letters.
distractorRationale.a: This counts only the letter arrangements.
distractorRationale.c: This uses the wrong number of letter choices.
